fields.content: We have traced your 503 overload errors and want to give you an accurate picture. They are two different responses. Most of the recent ones carry reason code GATEWAY_ADMISSION_OVERLOAD: the request is rejected at our gateway before it reaches routing, so fallback does not and cannot apply to them. A small number carry ROUTER_UPSTREAM_BREAKER_OPEN: for those, your configured same-region fallback between your two chat models is working and succeeding. We have not changed your fallback configuration, and fallback does not cover every 503. Our gateway and SRE teams are now investigating the admission thresholds and capacity behind the gateway rejections, and our routing team is verifying your existing fallback policy. In the meantime please honour the Retry-After header, retry with exponential backoff and jitter, cap retries, and avoid raising concurrency during a spike. Sharing x-redwood-correlation-id values, timestamps, region and model for recent failures will speed up the investigation. We will update you when the gateway investigation has findings. Broader fallback, such as cross-region or other model types, is outside your current order form; your account owner can discuss that if you want it.

fields.content: We have identified two different sources of overload 503s. Recent evidence shows most are gateway admission rejections, before requests reach Smart Routing, so routing fallback cannot handle those requests. Earlier tests and the available dashboard show your existing same-region fallback working for eligible router breaker-open events. Your recorded scope is fallback between two named chat models in the same region; we have not enabled global or cross-region fallback or expanded it to embeddings, rerank or other models. We have opened Gateway/SRE investigation of admission thresholds and capacity and asked Routing to verify the existing bounded policy. This is not yet a confirmed fix, and fallback does not cover every overload 503. Please respect Retry-After; if absent, use capped exponential backoff with jitter (for example 0.5, 1, 2, 4 seconds, at most four retries within your request deadline), and reduce concurrency rather than immediately retrying. Please share affected request/correlation IDs, timestamps with timezone, endpoint, model/region, response headers including Retry-After, retry settings and business impact. We will update you after the gateway investigation and policy verification. Basis: ATLAS-503-FALLBACK support evidence dated Nov 13, overload dashboard dated Nov 14, and recorded entitlement dated Nov 12.

fields.content: We reviewed the overload evidence for ATLAS-503-FALLBACK. The recent failures are gateway admission overloads (GATEWAY_ADMISSION_OVERLOAD), rejected before a routing decision is made. Routing fallback cannot handle these pre-routing rejections. Earlier router-breaker tests and the available dashboard evidence show that your configured same-region fallback does work for eligible ROUTER_UPSTREAM_BREAKER_OPEN events. Your recorded entitlement covers fallback between two approved chat models in the same region, not all models or regions. We have preserved that policy, not enabled global fallback. We have opened Gateway/SRE investigation of admission thresholds and capacity, Routing verification of the existing bounded policy, and confirmation of the exact approved model pair with the account team. Nordbank security questionnaire submission — 2026-11-14; deal NORDBANK-EU-27. Active scope: Hosted EU. For the proposed blanket statement that all content, logs, backups, operational metadata, support access and personnel remain EU-only, the answer is No: we cannot confirm that statement for the current Hosted EU scope. The approved responses below are deployment-specific, not acceptance of the broader contractual representation. Dedicated and Private are alternatives for evaluation only; neither has been approved for this deal. The broader clause remains open for Legal/GRC review; this submission does not amend or supersede the MSA/DPA.

HOSTED API – EU REGION

1) Where are prompts/inputs and model outputs processed (EU vs US)?
When a customer selects an EU region for Redwood Hosted, customer content (e.g., prompts/inputs and model outputs) is processed within the selected EU region for the purpose of serving the request.

2) Are prompts/outputs stored at rest by default? If yes, for how long and where?
By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts/inputs or model outputs to train foundation models. Storage and retention of customer content depend on the specific product configuration and customer agreement. Where storage is enabled for operational reasons (e.g., troubleshooting with customer approval), data is retained for a limited period and handled in accordance with Redwood’s data retention policy. Customers may request deletion as described in Redwood’s customer-facing retention/deletion overview.

3) Where are logs stored (application logs, audit logs, access logs)?
Redwood generates service logs and audit/security-relevant logs to operate the service (e.g., authentication events, administrative actions, and system health telemetry). Log storage and retention depend on deployment mode and customer configuration. Redwood can support EU-region deployments where logs and related operational data are stored and processed in the selected EU region.

4) Is any data replicated cross-region for DR/backups?
Redwood does not replicate customer content cross-region by default for EU-region deployments. Business continuity and disaster recovery controls are implemented at the service level; cross-region replication, if required, is handled only by explicit customer request/contracted configuration.

5) Can support staff outside the EU access our data (even transiently), and under what controls?
Redwood restricts internal access to customer data on a least-privilege basis. Where access is required for support or incident response, it is authorized, time-bound, and logged. Access may be performed by Redwood personnel located outside the EU, depending on the nature of the request and support coverage.

6) Dedicated vs Private deployments
Dedicated (EU region): For Redwood Dedicated provisioned in an EU region, inference processing occurs within the selected EU region. Data handling, logging, and retention controls are configurable and aligned to the contracted deployment architecture. Redwood does not replicate customer content cross-region by default; any cross-region configuration would be an explicit, contracted exception.

Private (VPC/on‑prem): For Redwood Private, the customer controls where the system runs (e.g., customer VPC or on-prem). Customer content is processed within the customer-controlled environment. Operational telemetry and support access can be configured to meet customer requirements; any access is governed by customer-approved controls and auditing.

Hello Helios Health team,

We are reviewing your December–February Dedicated throughput claim. The historical dashboard used streaming counters affected by a double-counting issue, so that dashboard alone cannot establish compliance. A change in the counter after the fix also does not by itself establish a change in delivered performance.

We have requested reconstruction using corrected accounting, verification of the applicable measurement rules and exclusions, and an SRE determination. We are also reviewing your contractual credit entitlement. We cannot yet confirm compliance, a breach, or a service-credit amount; the proposed 10% has not been approved.

Please confirm the exact December–February dates (including years and time zone), affected deployment IDs, endpoints/models, example request IDs and any relevant client logs through this support thread. We will follow up here once the technical and approval reviews are complete. Your claim remains open.

Customer Reliability and Credits
